description:
Once-only jobs start before their inputs exist, run, find the input missing,
wait, and run again when it arrives. Every function is defined twice.

Reduced case: `def main(), do: Enum.take([1, 2, 3], 2)` (see epic).
Paper: a per-function job whose inputs are fixed facts of that function runs
exactly once per subject: DefineFunction, LowerFunction, DeriveStaticCallees,
DeriveCallGraphComponent, ExpandFunctionSource, PlanEntryDispatch,
DeriveFunctionContract; DefineModule once per module.
Measured: DefineFunction 110 runs / 55 subjects, every re-run woken by
ExpandedFunctionSource; LowerFunction 112/60 (FunctionDefined);
DeriveStaticCallees 125/63 (LoweredBody); DeriveCallGraphComponent 53/36
(StaticCallees); DefineModule 15/5, one module 5 times (CodeIndexed,
CodeScoped).

Question to settle first (a reader, not a builder): who starts the first run
of each — the demand that reaches the job (pull), a blocked-waiter expansion,
or the activation frontier — and why it is started before the fact it reads
first is present. The first run's only product is a wait; its existence is
the defect.

Acceptance: the reduced case shows runs == subjects for every kind above; the
full-fixture job count drops; no pin rises.
title: Once-only jobs start before their inputs exist and run twice
